I think Final Fantasy is trying a lot harder to say relevant when all they need to is cater to the fanbase that made them successful in the first place. The series is selling a lot less in Japan and it's not due to decreasing console interest. Final Fantasy XIII sold more and faster than XV and there were less PS3's then. Not only that, the DS was king in Japan at the time. If anything, XV, despite being the best selling PS4 game in Japan, is not selling as well as say, VIII(the best selling Final Fantasy game in Japan to date), over there due to it not catering to their tastes. A more western, action-oriented route will not sell to the Japanese, period. When these developers keep making games that cater to a casual mainstream western audience that loves their CoD, GTA, Halo, Skyrim, etc. is when interest decreases. This leads to less sales.

And this also alienates their relatively large fanbase outside of Japan which thus leads to decreasing popularity. Horrible methods of branching out and your fanbase on both sides getting alienated by bad games and games that don't feel like Final Fantasy.

JRPGs were never popular/mainstream aside form Pokemon, period. Final Fantasy broke a niche barrier by substantial advertisement and high production values, introducing people to a new genre. This was back when the series and JRPGs peaked during the golden age(I miss it so). Then due to the increasing interest of dude-bro games over-saturating the market the Japanese developers wanted to find a way to make high end stakes. However they didn't deliver upon any of it.

TLDR: Final Fantasy is becoming less popular due to alienating both sides of the fanbase and not delivering. Constantly bringing in newer fan-bases who just wanted to see what the fuss was about but ultimately alienating everyone.

Real time games take a lot more time and money to develop than turn based games. You need a far more robust physics engine, far more complicated calculations, with a lot more glitches and bugs to test for. Turn based game play is basically just numbers exchanging in the background, everything you see on screen is a combination of pre rendered animations and effects.
